body.statement: On \(\mathcal P^{0,\mathrm{bin}}_{d,\epsilon,M}\), \(\tau(P)=\psi_1(P)\) because \(\mu_{0k}=0\) on every positive-mass cell. More explicitly, take the control-arm-zero binary hard family used in ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024, Theorem 2 and Appendix C.5, leave its zero control outcome fixed, and multiply its binary treated outcome by \(M\). The induced full-data laws belong to \(\mathcal P^{0,\mathrm{bin}}_{d,\epsilon,M}\subseteq\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}\), preserve cell masses and propensities, satisfy the fourth-central-moment envelope, and multiply both \(\psi_1\)-separation and ATE separation by \(M\). Consequently the theorem's one-arm mean-squared-error lower scale \(M^2\{n^{-1}+d^2/[n^2\log^2(en)]\}\) transfers by subclass restriction to ATE point estimation for \(d\lesssim_{\epsilon}n\log(en)\). Its priors may be used in \(thm:same-class-testing-converse\) only after that theorem separately proves ATE target-set separation and prior-predictive total-variation control.
body.justification: The source result concerns the treated-arm functional, so an explicit control-zero embedding is required before its rate can inform any ATE lower-bound argument.
body.gap: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024, Theorem 2 and Appendix C.5, lower-bound \(\psi_1\) and use a control-arm-zero proof family; the proposition records the exact subclass and scaling identity that transfer this source experiment to the ATE model without relabeling the published estimand.
body.consumer: The rare-cell source priors for the direct same-class confidence-length converse.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P^{0,\mathrm{bin}}_{d,\epsilon,M}\).  From
\(ass:control\text{-}arm\text{-}zero\text{-}subclass\) and consistency,
\(Y=0\) almost surely on \(\{A=0\}\).  Therefore, on every positive-mass
cell, \(\mu_{0k}=E_P[Y\mid A=0,X=k]=0\); the conditioning event has positive
probability because \(ass:fixed\text{-}overlap\) gives
\(P(A=0,X=k)=p_k(1-\pi_k)\ge\epsilon p_k>0\).  The identifying equality in
\(def:ate\text{-}functional\) now gives
\[
 \tau(P)=\sum_{k=1}^dp_k\mu_{1k}=\psi_1(P).
\tag{1}
\]

To verify the scaling rather than merely relabel the estimand, start with a
binary treated outcome \(B\in\{0,1\}\) in the hard family of
\(lem:zeng\text{-}one\text{-}arm\text{-}lower\), put \(Y(0)=0\), and put
\(Y(1)=MB\).  Leave \(X\), the cell masses, and the propensities unchanged,
and generate treatment conditionally independently of the potential outcomes
given \(X\).  This gives conditional exchangeability; defining
\(Y=Y(A)\) gives consistency.  Its cell means satisfy
\(0\le\mu_{1k}\le M\) and \(\mu_{0k}=0\).  Furthermore
\[
 |Y(1)-E[Y(1)\mid X=k]|\le M,
 \qquad Y(0)-E[Y(0)\mid X=k]=0,
\]
so every required conditional fourth central moment is at most \(M^4\).
Thus every scaled law lies in
\(\mathcal P^{0,\mathrm{bin}}_{d,\epsilon,M}\subseteq
\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}\).  Both sides of (1) are multiplied by \(M\),
and squared error is multiplied by \(M^2\).  The cited one-arm lower bound
therefore gives, by restricting the supremum from
\(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}\) to this subclass,
\[
 \inf_{\widehat\tau}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(\widehat\tau-\tau(P))^2]
 \ge c_\epsilon M^2\left\{n^{-1}+\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right\}
\]
throughout the source theorem's stated range.  This is a point-estimation
conclusion only.  Nothing in this reduction itself supplies two concentrated,
ATE-separated priors or controls their prior-predictive total variation, which
explains the final qualification in the proposition.
